seo.title: Dubai to UK Pet Move: The Tapeworm Window That Decides It
seo.meta_description: The single detail that gets dogs refused entry to the UK from Dubai: the tapeworm treatment must be given 24–120 hours before arrival. Here's how to get it right.
seo.og_title: The one timing rule that decides if your dog enters the UK

hero.h1: Dubai to the UK: the tapeworm window that decides if your dog flies
hero.standfirst: One mistimed treatment is the most common reason a Dubai → UK pet move fails. The fix is free — if you know the rule.
hero.image_alt: A dog ready to travel from Dubai to the UK

byline: By our relocation specialists · 9 June 2026 · reviewed by our IPATA-certified specialists
takeaways: Tapeworm treatment for dogs: 24–120 hours before arrival. Cats don't need it.
The UK health certificate must come from an APHA-approved vet — most Dubai vets aren't on that list.
Order matters: ISO microchip first, then the rabies vaccine (≥21 days before travel).
Banned breeds can't enter: Pit Bull, XL Bully (since 1 Feb 2024), Tosa, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro.
Do it right and there is no quarantine — the risk is paperwork, not quarantine.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: To bring a dog into the UK from Dubai, a vet must treat it for tapeworm no less than 24 hours and no more than 120 hours (5 days) before arrival — not earlier, not later. Miss that window and your dog is refused entry or held. Cats are exempt.
Get the microchip, rabies vaccine, APHA-approved health certificate and that tapeworm window right, and there's no quarantine — your dog clears and comes home the same day.

sections.heading: The tapeworm window, exactly
paragraphs: The UK requires a vet to treat your dog with an approved tapeworm product (containing praziquantel) and record it, no less than 24 hours and no more than 5 days before you enter Great Britain. Treat too early and the record is invalid; too late and your dog can't board or is held at the border.

Because the window is so tight, it has to be planned backwards from your exact flight — which is why the treatment is the last clinical step, not the first. Cats and ferrets are exempt; this is a dog-only rule.

sections.heading: Why your normal Dubai vet may not work
paragraphs: The UK health certificate for a pet arriving from the UAE must be issued by an APHA-approved (official) veterinarian. Many Dubai clinics aren't on that list, and a certificate from the wrong vet is rejected at the UK border.
Confirm your vet's approval before you book any appointment. This one check — vet approval plus the tapeworm timing — is what separates a smooth arrival from an expensive hold.

story.lead: The biggest cost on a Dubai → UK move is almost never the airline — it's one mistimed detail.
story.problem: An owner takes the cheapest quote for their Labrador, flying in three weeks.
story.mistake: The provider uses a vet who isn't APHA-approved and gives the tapeworm treatment a week early to 'be safe'.
story.discovery: At check-in the UK health certificate is rejected and the 24–120 hour window has lapsed — the dog can't board.
story.result: A rebooked flight, a fresh certificate and a few days of boarding add roughly AED 6,000 and over a week.
story.lesson: The cheapest quote cost the most. The APHA vet and the tapeworm window aren't details — they decide whether your dog flies.

faqs.q: Will my pet be quarantined when arriving in the UK?
faqs.a: No — pets that arrive with correct paperwork are not quarantined. The risk is a documentation or timing error, not routine quarantine.

faqs.q: Do I need a rabies blood test (titre) for the UK?
faqs.a: No. The UAE is a 'listed' country for the UK, so there's no rabies titre test or three-month wait — just a valid rabies vaccination at least 21 days before travel.

faqs.q: Does my cat need the tapeworm treatment?
faqs.a: No. The tapeworm rule applies to dogs only.

faqs.q: Can my XL Bully come to the UK?
faqs.a: No. The XL Bully has been banned since 1 February 2024, alongside Pit Bull, Japanese Tosa, Dogo Argentino and Fila Brasileiro. We verify your breed before booking.

method.structure_logic: 2026 article anatomy: headline (curiosity/result) -> answer-first opening (the liftable answer in the first lines) -> key takeaways -> table of contents -> scannable H2/H3 -> a visual (data table or flow) -> original insight or a story -> FAQ -> official sources -> one help-first CTA. Why: web readers scan ~20-28% of words (Nielsen Norman Group), so the answer is front-loaded; a story is remembered where bare facts are forgotten; one page = one job + a single CTA converts. These choices recur across every source in our research (see SOURCING-METHOD.md).
method.geo_seo_rationale: What we believe helps. GEO (being cited by AI answer engines): answer-first self-contained chunks, cited statistics, official-source citations, consistent entities, FAQ schema -- and citation is decoupled from ranking (~66% of AI-Overview citations come from outside the top-20), so strong content can be cited even before it ranks. SEO: intent-matched title+H1, topical depth, internal links into the money page, visible freshness dates, structured data (Article/FAQ/Breadcrumb/LocalBusiness). HONEST CAVEAT: these are evidence-based best practices, NOT guaranteed results -- ranking also needs off-page authority/backlinks/indexing not built here, and GEO citation is plausible but unproven until measured with a live AI-citation test.
method.how_and_why_we_audit: Each page is scored by a 5-lens auditor -- Website, SEO, GEO, Lead-gen/Trust, Quality -- which together cover the 7-category QA (Helpful, Human, Original, Trustworthy, SEO, GEO, Conversion). Why this way: (1) page-type profiles judge a page against ITS job (a reassurance page is weighted differently from a money page); (2) every check carries an evidence tier (T1 sworn -> T6 practitioner) and a verified-vs-heuristic tag; (3) not-measurable checks are excluded, never zeroed (a coverage->confidence label); (4) risk caps catch keyword-stuffing, thin content, fake schema, no-CTA. The score is an on-page QUALITY PROXY, not a measured ranking/citation outcome.
method.what_we_are_sure_of: 100% sure = a fact screenshot-verified against its official source as of a date (see sourcing.verified_100pct) + that the method was applied. NOT sure = that it ranks or gets cited (unproven until the site is live, indexed and measured).
method.how_we_verify: Every factual/regulatory claim is verified against an OFFICIAL source only -- government bodies, recognised standards bodies (IATA), or the operator's own site (e.g. the airline). Never blogs, forums, competitors, or AI. Each verified claim is captured as a full-page SCREENSHOT and logged in a regulatory register with: source, URL, date verified, version, reviewer, and a re-verify-by date (because regulations change). Anything we could not confirm from an official source is HEDGED or flagged 'confirm with [authority]', never asserted (see sourcing.stated_but_unverified). Tooling: a Playwright screenshot verifier with an official-domain allowlist + the regulatory register. Facts are kept separate from advice ('the authority requires X' vs 'we recommend X'). AI never makes the final call -- a human reviews and signs off before publish.
